quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Photo Caption That Omits Timing] The nonprofit's fundraising email features a photograph captioned 'children at our new school, built with your donations,' a building that records show was actually completed eighteen months before this particular fundraising campaign began, funded by an entirely separate, already-concluded grant, a detail the caption's phrasing does not make clear to a reader unfamiliar with the organization's project timeline.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the caption's relationship to this specific fundraising campaign?
options: The school was built after this fundraising campaign concluded.
It may create the impression that current donations funded this particular building, when records suggest otherwise.
The caption explicitly clarifies the funding came from an earlier, separate grant.
It accurately describes the school as built specifically with funds from this campaign.
quests.correctAnswer: It may create the impression that current donations funded this particular building, when records suggest otherwise.
quests.hint: Think about what a reader unfamiliar with the project timeline would likely assume from this caption, compared to what the records actually show.
quests.explanation: Since records show the school was completed well before this campaign began, using different funding, the caption's ambiguous phrasing most strongly supports the inference that it could mislead readers about which donations actually built the school.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Sleep Study's Selective Recruitment] The widely publicized sleep study finding that a particular bedtime routine improved sleep quality recruited its volunteer participants exclusively through an advertisement on a website dedicated to sleep optimization techniques, a recruitment method that a research methodology critic notes likely attracted people already motivated to follow structured routines carefully, a trait that could itself improve reported sleep outcomes independent of the specific routine being tested.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the study's findings?
options: The study recruited participants entirely at random from the general population.
The recruitment method has no bearing on how representative the results are.
The improvement may be partly attributable to participants' existing motivation and discipline rather than the specific routine alone.
The findings apply equally to people regardless of their existing habits or motivation.
quests.correctAnswer: The improvement may be partly attributable to participants' existing motivation and discipline rather than the specific routine alone.
quests.hint: Think about what recruiting exclusively from an already highly motivated audience supports about whether the routine itself, versus participants' existing traits, drove the improvement.
quests.explanation: Recruiting exclusively from a highly motivated audience most strongly supports the inference that the participants' existing discipline may have contributed to the improved outcomes, independent of the specific routine studied.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Grievance Process Rarely Used] The company's official employee handbook describes a detailed formal grievance process available to any employee with a workplace complaint, yet HR records requested through an internal audit show the process has been formally used only twice in the past decade, despite exit interview data indicating a much larger number of departing employees cited unresolved workplace concerns as a reason for leaving.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about this gap between available process and actual use?
options: Nearly every employee with a concern used the formal grievance process as intended.
Many employees with workplace concerns likely did not use the formal process, for reasons the passage does not specify.
The grievance process has never once been used in the company's history.
The exit interview data and the grievance records are certainly measuring the exact same set of concerns.
quests.correctAnswer: Many employees with workplace concerns likely did not use the formal process, for reasons the passage does not specify.
quests.hint: Notice that the passage establishes a gap between reported concerns and formal use, without stating why employees chose not to use the process.
quests.explanation: A large gap between reported workplace concerns and rare formal use of the grievance process most strongly supports the inference that many employees did not use the available process, though the passage does not specify why.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Restoration Photo Taken From One Angle] The 'before and after' photographs the historic preservation society displays to justify its renovation approach were taken from carefully chosen angles that a former board member, now critical of the project, says were selected specifically to make the original structure appear more deteriorated than photographs taken from other angles around the same time actually show.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the displayed 'before' photographs?
options: They represent the only photographic evidence of the structure's condition at that time.
They may present a more severe picture of deterioration than other available evidence from the same period would support.
Photographs from other angles show even greater deterioration than the displayed ones.
They were selected at random with no consideration of angle or framing.
quests.correctAnswer: They may present a more severe picture of deterioration than other available evidence from the same period would support.
quests.hint: Think about what a former board member's specific claim, that angles were chosen to exaggerate deterioration, supports about how representative these particular photos are.
quests.explanation: A former board member's account that specific angles were chosen to emphasize deterioration, compared to other photographs from the same period, most strongly supports the inference that the displayed images present a more severe picture than the fuller photographic record.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Carbon Label Calculated Narrowly] The product's package displays a carbon footprint label calculated only from emissions generated during final assembly, a scope that a lifecycle analysis expert notes excludes the considerably larger emissions generated earlier in extracting and processing the raw materials, a stage responsible, by industry-wide estimates, for the majority of most similar products' total lifecycle emissions.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about what this label actually represents?
options: Raw material extraction and processing generate negligible emissions for this category of product.
It represents the product's complete lifecycle carbon footprint from start to finish.
It likely represents a small fraction of the product's true total carbon footprint.
The label's scope has no bearing on how it should be interpreted by a shopper.
quests.correctAnswer: It likely represents a small fraction of the product's true total carbon footprint.
quests.hint: Think about what excluding the stage industry-wide estimates identify as generating the majority of emissions supports about how complete this label's figure really is.
quests.explanation: Excluding the lifecycle stage that industry estimates identify as generating most emissions for similar products most strongly supports the inference that the displayed label captures only a small fraction of the product's true total footprint.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [An App Permission Requested Beyond Its Function] The simple flashlight app requests permission to access the user's contacts, location, and microphone, none of which a security researcher notes are technically necessary for a flashlight application's stated function, though the app's privacy policy describes these permissions only as being used to 'enhance the user experience' without further detail.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the purpose of these permission requests?
options: The security researcher confirmed these permissions are used exclusively to improve battery life.
They are all technically required for a flashlight app to function properly.
The privacy policy provides a complete, specific explanation of each permission's use.
They likely serve purposes beyond what is described, given they exceed what the app's basic function requires.
quests.correctAnswer: They likely serve purposes beyond what is described, given they exceed what the app's basic function requires.
quests.hint: Think about what requesting permissions unnecessary for the stated function, combined with only a vague explanation, supports about what those permissions might actually be used for.
quests.explanation: Permissions unnecessary for a flashlight's basic function, paired with only a vague 'enhance the user experience' explanation, most strongly supports the inference that these permissions likely serve some undisclosed purpose beyond the app's stated function.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Clinical Advisory Board With Financial Ties] Six of the eight physicians serving on the medical device company's clinical advisory board, tasked with reviewing safety data, also receive separate paid consulting fees from the same company for unrelated speaking engagements, an overlap disclosed only in a footnote of a conference presentation rather than in the board's own published safety reviews.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the advisory board's safety reviews?
options: The financial ties are irrelevant to how the reviews should be evaluated.
The reviews are certainly compromised and their conclusions are definitely inaccurate.
The overlap was prominently disclosed within the safety reviews themselves.
There may be a reasonable basis for questioning how independent these particular reviews are, given the undisclosed financial ties.
quests.correctAnswer: There may be a reasonable basis for questioning how independent these particular reviews are, given the undisclosed financial ties.
quests.hint: Distinguish between a financial relationship creating reasonable grounds for scrutiny and it proving the reviews themselves are false.
quests.explanation: An undisclosed financial relationship between most board members and the company creates a reasonable basis for questioning independence, a more measured inference than assuming the reviews are definitely inaccurate.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Productivity App's Selective Statistics] The time-tracking app's marketing claims users complete tasks '35 percent faster' after adopting its system, a figure calculated only from users who continued using the app for at least six months, excluding from the calculation the substantial majority of downloaders who, according to the company's own retention data disclosed separately to investors, stopped using the app within the first month.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the 35 percent figure's relevance to a typical new user?
options: It accurately represents the typical experience of everyone who downloads the app.
The retention data has no bearing on how this marketing figure should be interpreted.
It may not represent the experience of most people who try the app, since it excludes the majority who stopped using it early.
Most downloaders continued using the app for at least six months.
quests.correctAnswer: It may not represent the experience of most people who try the app, since it excludes the majority who stopped using it early.
quests.hint: Think about what excluding the majority of early-quitting users, likely a group less representative of strong results, does to how representative the remaining figure is.
quests.explanation: Since the figure excludes the majority who quit within a month, likely a group less representative of strong results, the most supported inference is that this statistic may not reflect a typical new user's actual experience.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Manufacturing Defect Downplayed in Language] The automaker's internal engineering memo describes a component failure mode discovered during testing as an 'edge-case anomaly under atypical conditions,' language that, according to a former company engineer who reviewed the memo, corresponded to failure conditions that internal test data showed occurring in roughly one of every four hundred vehicles under normal daily driving, not the rare, unusual circumstances the phrasing implies.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the memo's description of this issue?
options: The failure occurred only under conditions engineers would consider highly unusual.
The phrasing accurately reflects how rare this failure was in practice.
The chosen language likely understates how commonly this failure actually occurred under normal conditions.
The internal test data showed this failure never occurred under normal driving.
quests.correctAnswer: The chosen language likely understates how commonly this failure actually occurred under normal conditions.
quests.hint: Compare the phrase 'edge-case anomaly under atypical conditions' with the actual one-in-four-hundred frequency described under normal driving.
quests.explanation: A failure rate of one in four hundred vehicles under normal driving, contrasted with language suggesting rare and unusual conditions, most strongly supports the inference that the memo's phrasing understates how commonly this issue actually occurred.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Ceasefire Described Differently by Each Side] Following the ceasefire agreement, one government's official statement describes the outcome as a 'complete victory achieving all strategic objectives,' while the opposing government's statement describes the same agreement as a 'necessary pause achieved on our own terms,' each framing offered to a domestic audience without any acknowledgment of the other side's account.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about these two official descriptions?
options: One of the two descriptions has been independently confirmed as the accurate one by this passage.
The two governments jointly agreed on how the outcome would be described.
Each government is likely presenting the outcome in the way most favorable to its own domestic audience, rather than offering a neutral account.
Both descriptions are equally objective and neutral accounts of the same event.
quests.correctAnswer: Each government is likely presenting the outcome in the way most favorable to its own domestic audience, rather than offering a neutral account.
quests.hint: Think about what two starkly different framings, each directed at that government's own domestic audience, suggest about the neutrality of either account on its own.
quests.explanation: Two contrasting, self-favorable framings, each aimed at a domestic audience, most strongly support the inference that neither official statement alone offers a neutral, complete account of the actual outcome.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Water Rights Agreement Measured by One Number] Officials announce that a new water-sharing agreement between two regions increases the downstream region's allocated share by 20 percent, a figure that does not address a separate provision, noted only in the agreement's technical appendix, allowing the upstream region to build additional reservoir capacity that hydrologists say could reduce total downstream flow regardless of the percentage allocation.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the practical effect of this agreement on downstream water availability?
options: Hydrologists confirmed the agreement will definitely increase total downstream flow.
The 20 percent figure guarantees a proportional increase in actual downstream water availability.
The headline 20 percent figure alone may not accurately predict the actual amount of water reaching the downstream region.
The reservoir provision has no possible effect on downstream flow.
quests.correctAnswer: The headline 20 percent figure alone may not accurately predict the actual amount of water reaching the downstream region.
quests.hint: Think about what a separate provision allowing more upstream reservoir capacity, which hydrologists say could reduce downstream flow, does to the reliability of the headline percentage alone.
quests.explanation: A separate provision that could reduce total downstream flow, according to hydrologists, most strongly supports the inference that the headline allocation percentage alone may not accurately predict actual water availability downstream.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Recycling Symbol That Doesn't Guarantee Recycling] The plastic container displays a widely recognized triangular recycling symbol with the number 7 inside, a code that, according to waste management specialists, actually designates a mixed category of plastics that most municipal recycling programs, including the one serving the area where this product is primarily sold, do not currently have the capability to process.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about what happens to this container after a consumer places it in a recycling bin?
options: It likely is not actually recycled by most local programs, despite bearing a recycling symbol.
This specific area's recycling program can definitely process this category of plastic.
It is guaranteed to be recycled because it displays the triangular symbol.
The number 7 designation guarantees compatibility with all municipal recycling programs.
quests.correctAnswer: It likely is not actually recycled by most local programs, despite bearing a recycling symbol.
quests.hint: Think about what specialists' statement, that most programs including this specific area's cannot process category 7 plastics, supports about what actually happens to this container.
quests.explanation: Specialists' statement that the local program cannot process category 7 plastics most strongly supports the inference that this container likely is not actually recycled despite displaying the recognizable symbol.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Grant Recipient List That Favors Insiders] An analysis of the charitable foundation's grant recipients over five years finds that organizations with a board member who previously worked at the foundation received grants at a rate more than three times higher than comparable organizations without such a connection, a pattern the foundation's public statement attributes to 'the strength of those particular applications' without addressing the connection itself.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the foundation's grant-making pattern?
options: The foundation's statement has fully and directly addressed why this pattern exists.
Organizations with a connected board member never receive grants.
Application quality alone, with no connection to any relationship, fully explains the tripled rate.
Personal connections to the foundation may be playing a meaningful role in grant decisions, beyond application quality alone.
quests.correctAnswer: Personal connections to the foundation may be playing a meaningful role in grant decisions, beyond application quality alone.
quests.hint: Think about what a tripled grant rate, combined with a response that doesn't address the connection itself, supports about whether personal ties might be playing some role.
quests.explanation: A markedly higher grant rate for connected organizations, paired with a response that sidesteps the connection itself, most strongly supports the inference that personal ties may play a meaningful role, beyond what the foundation's stated explanation addresses.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Return-to-Office Mandate Justified by Anecdote] The company's leadership justifies its new full-time return-to-office mandate by citing 'countless examples' of improved collaboration since implementation, a claim the company has not paired with any internal survey, productivity metric, or comparative data, according to an employee who requested such supporting information through an internal feedback channel and received no response addressing the request directly.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the evidentiary basis for this justification?
options: The claim is backed by extensive internal survey and productivity data.
The claim of improved collaboration appears to rest on anecdote rather than any documented, measurable evidence presented so far.
The employee's request for data was answered with detailed supporting evidence.
No collaboration has occurred since the mandate was implemented.
quests.correctAnswer: The claim of improved collaboration appears to rest on anecdote rather than any documented, measurable evidence presented so far.
quests.hint: Think about what the absence of any survey, metric, or direct response to a data request supports about how well-substantiated this claim currently is.
quests.explanation: The absence of any cited survey, metric, or direct response to a specific request for evidence most strongly supports the inference that this claim currently rests on anecdote rather than documented data, at least based on what is described here.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Wellness App's Data Sharing, Clarified Slowly] Only after a class-action lawsuit does the period-tracking app's parent company clarify, in a court filing rather than any user-facing communication, that anonymized user data had been shared with third-party advertising partners since the app's launch, a practice the app's original privacy policy described only in a general clause about sharing data 'to improve services and for other business purposes.'
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about how clearly this data-sharing practice was originally communicated to users?
options: It was clearly and specifically disclosed to users in the original privacy policy.
It was likely not communicated in a way most users would have understood to include sharing with advertising partners.
The company voluntarily clarified this practice before any legal action was filed.
No data sharing of any kind occurred until after the lawsuit was filed.
quests.correctAnswer: It was likely not communicated in a way most users would have understood to include sharing with advertising partners.
quests.hint: Think about what a vague clause about 'other business purposes,' only clarified in a court filing after a lawsuit, supports about how clearly users were originally informed.
quests.explanation: A vague original clause, clarified specifically only within a court filing prompted by litigation, most strongly supports the inference that users were unlikely to have understood the original policy as covering advertising data-sharing.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Festival Attendance Figure Counted Generously] Organizers announce the annual festival drew 'over 100,000 attendees,' a figure a local transit authority's own ticket and parking data suggests significantly overstates actual unique visitors, since the organizers' count method, according to a city auditor's report, tallies each individual's entry and any re-entry throughout the multi-day event as a separate attendee.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the true number of unique individuals who attended?
options: It is likely higher than the 100,000 figure once re-entries are considered.
It is likely meaningfully lower than the 100,000 figure, given how re-entries are counted.
The transit authority's data confirms the organizers' figure is completely accurate.
It matches the 100,000 figure precisely, since re-entries do not affect the count.
quests.correctAnswer: It is likely meaningfully lower than the 100,000 figure, given how re-entries are counted.
quests.hint: Think about what counting each re-entry as a new attendee, rather than tracking unique individuals, does to a headline number like this one.
quests.explanation: Counting re-entries as separate attendees, rather than tracking unique individuals, most strongly supports the inference that the true number of distinct people who attended is likely meaningfully lower than the reported figure.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Translation App's Confident Error] The translation app renders a nuanced legal term in the source contract with a single, confident-sounding English equivalent, giving no indication to the reader that professional legal translators specializing in this exact language pair generally note the term has no precise one-word equivalent and typically requires an explanatory phrase to convey its full legal meaning accurately.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the app's translated output in this instance?
options: It likely conveys a false sense of precision that may not fully capture the term's actual legal meaning.
The term in question has a universally agreed-upon single-word English equivalent.
Professional translators agree a single-word translation is the standard, accepted approach for this term.
It accurately captures the complete legal nuance professional translators describe.
quests.correctAnswer: It likely conveys a false sense of precision that may not fully capture the term's actual legal meaning.
quests.hint: Think about what professional translators' description of this term needing an explanatory phrase supports about the reliability of the app's single confident word.
quests.explanation: Professional translators' assessment that this term requires an explanatory phrase, not a single word, most strongly supports the inference that the app's confident single-word rendering likely conveys a false sense of precision.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Wearable's Sleep Stage Claims] The sleep-tracking wearable's app displays detailed graphs breaking a night's sleep into precise percentages of light, deep, and REM sleep stages, a level of granularity that sleep researchers note current consumer-grade wrist sensors are not capable of measuring directly, since accurately distinguishing these stages typically requires brainwave monitoring equipment the wearable does not include.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the accuracy of these detailed sleep stage percentages?
options: The device includes brainwave monitoring equipment capable of this precision.
They are directly and precisely measured using the wearable's built-in sensors.
Sleep researchers confirmed this level of granular accuracy is achievable with wrist sensors alone.
They are likely estimates rather than direct, precise measurements of actual sleep stages.
quests.correctAnswer: They are likely estimates rather than direct, precise measurements of actual sleep stages.
quests.hint: Think about what researchers' statement, that this precision requires equipment the wearable lacks, supports about whether the displayed percentages reflect direct measurement or something else.
quests.explanation: Researchers noting that this precision requires brainwave equipment the wearable does not include most strongly supports the inference that the displayed percentages are estimates rather than direct, measured readings.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Founder's Story Simplified for Investors] The startup founder's pitch deck describes the company's origin as a solo effort born from personal frustration with an existing product, a narrative that court records from an unrelated dispute later reveal omits two co-founders who left the company early and whose initial technical contributions, according to those same records, formed the basis of the product's core early architecture.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the pitch deck's origin story?
options: The departed co-founders made no meaningful contribution to the product's early architecture.
It likely simplifies the company's actual founding in a way that omits significant early contributions from others.
Court records confirm the solo-founder narrative in every detail.
It fully and accurately reflects everyone involved in the company's founding.
quests.correctAnswer: It likely simplifies the company's actual founding in a way that omits significant early contributions from others.
quests.hint: Think about what court records revealing omitted co-founders and their architectural contributions support about how complete the pitch deck's simplified story really is.
quests.explanation: Court records revealing omitted co-founders whose work formed the product's core early architecture most strongly supports the inference that the solo-founder narrative simplifies the actual history in a way that leaves out significant contributions.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Tipping Custom Explained Differently by Generations] Younger residents of the town describe the local custom of leaving a small coin, rather than paper currency, as a tip as simply 'how it's done here,' while a handful of the town's oldest residents recall the practice originating from a decades-old, now largely forgotten dispute between local workers and business owners over payment methods, a history absent from how younger residents describe or understand the custom today.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the custom as understood by most of the town's current residents?
options: The custom has no actual documented historical origin at all.
Most current residents are well aware of the custom's specific historical origin.
The younger residents' account and the older residents' account fully agree on the custom's origin.
It is likely now practiced without most people knowing or considering its original historical origin.
quests.correctAnswer: It is likely now practiced without most people knowing or considering its original historical origin.
quests.hint: Think about what younger residents describing the custom simply as tradition, with no mention of the dispute the oldest residents recall, supports about how widely that origin is remembered today.
quests.explanation: Younger residents describing the custom simply as tradition, without reference to the dispute the oldest residents recall, most strongly supports the inference that most current practitioners are likely unaware of its original historical context.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Salary Range Posted but Not Meant] The job posting lists a salary range of $70,000 to $95,000, complying with a new regional pay-transparency law, though a recruiter for the company later tells an applicant candidly that the company 'almost never' offers above the range's minimum regardless of a candidate's experience, a practice the recruiter describes as fairly common since the law took effect.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the practical meaning of the posted salary range in this case?
options: The posted range has no connection to what the company actually intends to pay.
Candidates can reliably expect an offer anywhere within the full posted range based on experience.
The upper portion of the range may not reflect what most candidates can realistically expect to be offered.
The company always offers the maximum figure in the posted range.
quests.correctAnswer: The upper portion of the range may not reflect what most candidates can realistically expect to be offered.
quests.hint: Think about what a recruiter's candid admission, that offers 'almost never' exceed the minimum, supports about how representative the full posted range actually is.
quests.explanation: A recruiter's candid admission that offers almost never exceed the range's minimum most strongly supports the inference that the upper portion of the posted range may not reflect realistic expectations for most candidates.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Wildlife Count Conducted Once a Year] Conservationists report a 'stable' population of a migratory bird species based on a single annual count conducted during a two-week window each spring, a methodology an independent ornithologist notes may miss significant fluctuations occurring at other points in the migratory cycle, since a population appearing stable during this specific window could still be declining or increasing substantially during other seasons not captured by the count.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the confidence that should be placed in the 'stable' designation?
options: It should be treated with some caution, since the counting method captures only a narrow window of the full annual cycle.
The counting method captures fluctuations across the entire migratory cycle.
It definitely means the population is declining during other seasons.
It can be fully trusted as an accurate reflection of the population across the entire year.
quests.correctAnswer: It should be treated with some caution, since the counting method captures only a narrow window of the full annual cycle.
quests.hint: Think about what a narrow two-week counting window, which an ornithologist says may miss fluctuations elsewhere in the cycle, supports about how confidently 'stable' can be applied to the whole year.
quests.explanation: An ornithologist's observation that a narrow annual window may miss fluctuations elsewhere in the cycle most strongly supports treating the 'stable' designation with some caution, rather than either fully trusting it or assuming decline.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Clinical Trial Description That Omits a Comparison] The medical device company's marketing describes trial results showing patients 'improved significantly' after using the device, a summary that a biostatistician reviewing the full published study notes omits that a comparison group receiving a lower-cost standard treatment showed statistically similar improvement, a detail relegated to a supplementary table in the original paper rather than the study's abstract.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about how the device's benefit compares to the standard treatment?
options: The device's improvement may not be meaningfully different from what the standard treatment already achieves.
The standard treatment showed no improvement whatsoever in the comparison group.
The device clearly outperforms the standard treatment by a wide margin.
The supplementary table data contradicts everything else reported in the study.
quests.correctAnswer: The device's improvement may not be meaningfully different from what the standard treatment already achieves.
quests.hint: Think about what a biostatistician's finding, that the comparison group showed 'statistically similar' improvement, supports about how the device's benefit truly compares to the cheaper alternative.
quests.explanation: A biostatistician's finding that the standard-treatment comparison group showed statistically similar improvement most strongly supports the inference that the device's benefit may not be meaningfully greater than the existing, lower-cost option.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Smart Home Device That Listens Longer Than Stated] The smart speaker's privacy policy states it 'only processes audio after the wake word is detected,' language that independent security researchers testing the device found to be accurate in most cases, though the same researchers documented a measurable number of instances where the device began recording and transmitting audio data without any wake word being spoken at all.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the accuracy of the privacy policy's description?
options: The researchers found no instances of the device recording without a wake word.
It appears to describe the device's typical behavior but not to fully capture certain documented exceptions.
It is entirely false, since the device never actually responds to the wake word.
It is completely accurate in every single instance without exception.
quests.correctAnswer: It appears to describe the device's typical behavior but not to fully capture certain documented exceptions.
quests.hint: Think about what researchers finding the policy 'accurate in most cases' but also documenting exceptions supports about how completely the policy describes actual behavior.
quests.explanation: Researchers confirming general accuracy while also documenting specific exceptions most strongly supports the inference that the policy captures typical behavior but not every documented case.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A National Ranking That Depends on the Measure] The country ranks first in the world on a widely cited 'quality of life' index, a ranking that weighs heavily toward measures like average income and infrastructure spending, while ranking considerably lower on a separate, less publicized index focused specifically on measures of work-life balance and mental health support, a discrepancy that index methodology experts attribute to the two rankings simply measuring different things.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about what the widely cited top ranking actually captures?
options: The lower ranking on the other index proves the top ranking is fabricated.
It comprehensively captures every meaningful dimension of quality of life, including work-life balance.
The two indexes are measuring identical things and should produce identical rankings.
It likely reflects certain specific measures, such as income and infrastructure, more than a comprehensive picture of overall wellbeing.
quests.correctAnswer: It likely reflects certain specific measures, such as income and infrastructure, more than a comprehensive picture of overall wellbeing.
quests.hint: Think about what experts' explanation, that the two indexes measure different things, supports about what the widely cited ranking specifically emphasizes.
quests.explanation: Experts' explanation that the two indexes measure different things most strongly supports the inference that the widely cited ranking reflects certain specific, heavily weighted measures rather than a comprehensive account of overall wellbeing.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Layoff Selection Criteria Left Unexplained] During a company-wide reduction in force, employees selected for layoff skew disproportionately toward those who took extended parental or medical leave within the past two years, a pattern an employment attorney reviewing the anonymized data describes as 'worth further investigation,' while cautioning that the data alone, without knowing the specific selection criteria actually used, cannot definitively establish why this pattern occurred.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported by the attorney's assessment?
options: The pattern is purely coincidental and warrants no further examination.
The specific selection criteria have already been fully disclosed and explained in the passage.
The pattern raises a legitimate question worth examining further, without the data alone proving a specific cause.
The data conclusively proves the layoffs were based on leave status.
quests.correctAnswer: The pattern raises a legitimate question worth examining further, without the data alone proving a specific cause.
quests.hint: Notice that the attorney's own words draw a distinction between a pattern worth investigating and a pattern that has been proven to have a specific cause.
quests.explanation: The attorney's own description, calling the pattern worth investigating while explicitly noting the data alone cannot establish a definitive cause, most strongly supports a measured inference between unproven suspicion and confirmed conclusion.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Textbook's Framing of a Contested Event] Textbooks used in two neighboring countries describe the same historical border conflict in starkly different terms, one framing the outcome as a justified reclaiming of ancestral territory and the other as an unprovoked act of aggression, with historians noting that both accounts selectively emphasize certain documented events while omitting others that would complicate their respective national narratives.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about these two textbook accounts?
options: One of the two accounts has been confirmed by historians as the fully accurate version.
Both accounts include every relevant documented event without omission.
Historians agree completely with one nation's specific framing over the other's.
Neither account, on its own, likely offers a complete picture of the historical events, since both appear to be selectively framed.
quests.correctAnswer: Neither account, on its own, likely offers a complete picture of the historical events, since both appear to be selectively framed.
quests.hint: Think about what historians' observation, that both accounts selectively emphasize and omit different events, supports about relying on either single textbook alone.
quests.explanation: Historians' observation that both accounts selectively emphasize certain events while omitting others most strongly supports the inference that neither single textbook, on its own, offers a complete account of the historical events.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Clinical Term Softened for Marketing] The cosmetic procedure's marketing materials describe potential side effects as 'temporary adjustments some patients experience,' phrasing a dermatologist reviewing the materials notes describes what the procedure's own FDA-mandated patient information sheet, provided separately and not featured in the marketing itself, lists explicitly as swelling, bruising, and in rare documented cases, prolonged numbness lasting several months.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the marketing materials' description of side effects?
options: The FDA-mandated sheet and the marketing description use identical language.
It uses more clinically specific language than the official patient information sheet.
It fully lists every specific side effect included in the official patient information.
It likely presents these effects in softer, less specific terms than the more detailed official patient information does.
quests.correctAnswer: It likely presents these effects in softer, less specific terms than the more detailed official patient information does.
quests.hint: Compare the vague phrase 'temporary adjustments' with the specific list of effects, including prolonged numbness, found in the separate official document.
quests.explanation: A vague marketing phrase standing in for a specific list that includes swelling, bruising, and prolonged numbness most strongly supports the inference that the marketing materials soften the description compared to the official patient information.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Startup Metric That Changes Definition] The company's reported 'active user' count remains steady across three consecutive quarterly investor updates, a stability that becomes less reassuring upon noticing that the definition of 'active user' was quietly broadened in the second quarter to include anyone who received a notification, not just those who opened the app, a methodological change the updates do not mention alongside the reported figures.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the apparent stability in this reported metric?
options: It certainly reflects genuinely stable engagement with no methodological influence.
The definition of 'active user' became narrower, not broader, during this period.
The updates clearly disclosed the definitional change alongside the figures.
It may partly reflect a change in what counts as an 'active user' rather than genuinely stable underlying engagement.
quests.correctAnswer: It may partly reflect a change in what counts as an 'active user' rather than genuinely stable underlying engagement.
quests.hint: Think about what broadening the definition of 'active user,' without disclosing the change, would do to a metric that might otherwise have declined.
quests.explanation: An undisclosed broadening of the 'active user' definition, occurring right as the metric needed to look stable, most strongly supports the inference that the apparent stability may partly reflect this definitional change rather than genuine underlying engagement.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Regulatory Filing That Reveals a Different Story] The company's public marketing describes its growth strategy as 'organic and customer-driven,' language that stands in some tension with a separate regulatory filing, required for an unrelated purpose, in which the same company describes a significant portion of its recent user growth as resulting from a paid acquisition partnership with a much larger platform, a detail not mentioned anywhere in the public marketing materials.
quests.question: Which inference is most strongly supported about the completeness of the public 'organic and customer-driven' description?
options: The regulatory filing confirms that all growth was entirely organic.
The paid acquisition partnership is prominently featured in the public marketing.
It likely omits a significant growth factor that the company itself describes differently in a separate required filing.
It fully aligns with everything disclosed in the regulatory filing.
quests.correctAnswer: It likely omits a significant growth factor that the company itself describes differently in a separate required filing.
quests.hint: Think about what a separate, differently framed account in a required filing, one the company had less discretion to shape for marketing purposes, supports about the completeness of the public description.
quests.explanation: A separate regulatory filing attributing significant growth to a paid partnership, a detail entirely absent from the public marketing, most strongly supports the inference that the public 'organic' framing omits a significant part of the actual growth story.
